Both are already linked to 88 common concepts, including fourier domain, hemoglobin and volumetric imaging, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses fourier domain as a bridge: first, review how brain imaging and linear array are each currently treated through fourier domain; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
medicine-436-2451.phd: A 3-4 year programme building a unified framework for brain imaging and linear array. Year 1: systematic review of the 88 shared concepts (starting with fourier domain, hemoglobin and volumetric imaging); years 2-3: develop and validate a joint method; year 4: generalise it and release open tools and data.
medicine-436-2451.masters: A 6-12 month project: reproduce one recent brain imaging study and one recent linear array study, then run a focused experiment combining the two through fourier domain, reporting what transfers and what does not.
